## 2026-07-05 — AirFRANS pilot: first contact, and a sharp error signature {#sec-nb-airfrans-pilot}

The scarce-task pilot (protocol-v0: flat AdamW 3e-4, 1,000 epochs =
GLOBE's actual budget, 4,096 queries/step, full boundary) completed
three of four arms; `mt_nl_pseudo` was walltime-killed at epoch 892
(it runs ~16 s/epoch vs ~12 for the others — resume support being
added). First-shot z-score MSEs on the published comparison surface,
seed 17 (seed 18 for `mt_nl` within ~10% on all volume fields):

| field | `mt_nl` | best Bonnet baseline | Transolver | MARIO | GLOBE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $u_x$ | 0.137 | 0.0146 | 0.0211 | 0.0015 | 0.00021 |
| $p$ (volume) | **0.0182** | 0.0329 | 0.0443 | 0.0024 | 0.00029 |
| $p$ (surface) | 1.25 | 0.147 | 0.237 | 0.027 | 0.00039 |

Two reads, both provisional (single seed, untuned schedule):

- **Volume pressure beats every Bonnet baseline and Transolver at
  first shot.** The kernel dictionary's pressure story survives its
  first industrial contact.
- **Velocity and surface pressure lag ~9×** — and the signature
  (good in the volume, bad at the wall; `mt_nl_decay` ≈ `mt_nl`, so
  it's not far-field) points at a *mechanistic* suspect: at
  $\mathrm{Re}\sim4\times10^6$ the boundary layer lives at
  $\delta/c \sim \mathrm{Re}^{-1/2} \approx 5\times10^{-4}$. GLOBE's
  kernels receive that scale directly (its second reference length
  $\delta_{FS}$ enters the radial pair features); ours must
  synthesize it from a chord-scale radial argument conditioned by a
  global $\ln\mathrm{Re}$ scalar. Hypothesis (logged before the
  diagnostic): the velocity error concentrates in the
  $d/c < 10^{-3}$ bands. The decisive test is a distance-banded
  eval decomposition, runnable from the saved checkpoints without
  retraining; if confirmed, the admissible fix is a *declared
  viscous scale* — a second similarity-covariant radial feature
  $r/(L_{\mathrm{ref}}\,\mathrm{Re}^{-1/2})$, which is a per-problem
  contract in exactly the program's sense, not a special case.

## 2026-07-05 — the banded diagnostic fires: it's the wall, quantified {#sec-nb-airfrans-bands}

The distance-banded eval of the pilot checkpoints (no retraining; 240 s
for all three) tests the logged hypothesis. Verdict: **confirmed in
weight, with an instructive tail.** For `mt_nl` seed 17, velocity
z-score MSE by band of $d/c$:

| band | $[0,10^{-4})$ | $[10^{-4},10^{-3})$ | $[10^{-3},10^{-2})$ | $[10^{-2},10^{-1})$ | $[0.1,1)$ | $[1,\infty)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $u_x$ MSE | **0.538** | 0.090 | 0.174 | 0.088 | 0.019 | 0.006 |
| $\|\Delta U\|/\|U_\infty\|$ MAE | 0.383 | 0.160 | 0.184 | 0.122 | 0.066 | 0.039 |

Contribution-weighted: the innermost band holds **49% of total
velocity MSE on 12.5% of points** (per-point error ~30× the
$[0.1,1)$ band); everything below $d/c=10^{-3}$ holds ~60%. The
profile replicates across seed 18 (band0 0.566) and the decay arm
(0.692) — architecture, not noise. The instructive tail: a secondary
hump in $[10^{-3},10^{-2})$ (outer boundary layer / near wake,
~0.15–0.19 in every run) says the deficit is *multi-scale*, not just
the sublayer — consistent with the GLOBE lineage's multi-scale kernel
motivation. Volume pressure shows the same shape at 10× lower level
(band0 0.082, elsewhere ≤0.016), which also explains the bad
*surface*-pressure headline: it is the band0 restriction of a field
that is fine everywhere else.

Next experiment pre-registered in the chapter (H4): **declared
auxiliary length scales** — per-problem similarity-covariant kernel
scales (the viscous $\delta/c = \mathrm{Re}^{-1/2}$ declared from
inputs), entering the pair features as additional
$r/\delta$-normalized invariants. Acceptance: ≥2× reduction of band-0
velocity MSE vs `mt_nl` at 3 seeds under protocol-v1, no regression in
outer bands. The protocol-v1 3-seed campaign (11 runs, GLOBE-endpoint
cosine) is training concurrently.

## 2026-07-06 — DrivAerML: the drive-stream overflow, and the pilot launch {#sec-nb-drivaer-smoke}

The five-boundary smoke's step-1 NaN root-caused to something worth
recording as a *model* lesson, not a pipeline bug: the zero-preserving
drive stream is **norm-free by construction** (an RMSNorm would break
the zero-drive ⇒ zero-output contract), so its operating magnitude is
set entirely by the inputs — and the recipe fed it two multiplicative
amplifiers at once. The declared freestream arrived as a *raw physical*
38.9 m/s (the recipe's nondimensionalizer never touches
`global_data`), and the tunnel-scale source coordinates (|x| ≈ 16
gauge units under the vehicle-scale gauge) blew the drive-block score
products to 6×10²³ → inf → NaN. A measured gauge dose-response (NaN at
gauge 1 → healthy 0.46 at gauge 8 — and the intrinsic merged-boundary
RMS radius is 8.54, landing exactly in the healthy regime) pinned the
fix: a derived unit `U_inf_dir` drive plus gauge 8 (= 40 m, tunnel
scale), identical across arms. A regression test with teeth (old
config: 4000/4000 non-finite; new: 0) pins it. Bonus finding: the
"clean" vehicle-only smoke had been training out of an O(10⁹) init
for the same reason — both arms improve. The 9× allbc slowdown was
the 165.8M-point volume interior riding through the early transforms
(the `.pdmsh` interior is a point *cloud*, so the cells-only reader
cap never touched it) — re-target-first ordering plus a points cap
fixed it (14 vs 15 min/epoch, arms matched).

Smoke v6: both arms finite from step 1, checkpointed, complete.
**Pilot launched** (jobs 4127442/43): both arms, 4-GPU DDP, recipe
default 500 epochs, `sampling_resolution=10000` (wall-clock-bound
dense decode; identical across arms so H-ground is unaffected;
absolute cross-model numbers carry the resolution caveat), ~29 h
each. The H-ground verdict — do the four labeled tunnel boundaries
beat shape-only? — lands when they do.

## 2026-07-06 — a convention audit, and the scale-completeness insight {#sec-nb-convention-scales}

**Convention audit (Peter's catch, confirmed against GLOBE's benchmark
source).** The published AirFRANS tables are per-sample z-scores of the
*nondimensional* fields: each sample's error divided by the std of
*that sample's* true field, averaged over samples (GLOBE's
`benchmark.py`, which also documents that the AirFRANS *paper* claims
freestream normalization while the AirFRANS *code* implements the
z-score scheme). Our eval used train-split-pooled std of *raw physical*
fields — a different measure. Every cross-table comparison logged so
far is therefore convention-mismatched, direction unknown until
re-scored (the pooled σ_u ≈ 29 m/s is inflated by the across-case
freestream spread; per-sample σ of U/|U∞| is ~4× smaller in relative
terms — the two effects pull opposite ways). The reference convention
is being ported exactly, with a with-teeth identity test (per-sample
mean predictor ⇒ z-score MSE ≡ 1.0), and all finished checkpoints get
re-scored eval-only. Until then, the published-table comparisons in
the two preceding entries are provisional. Within-program arm
comparisons (H2 confirmed, H3 refuted, band structure) are unaffected
— same convention on both sides.

**The scale-completeness insight (Peter, discussing H4).** Declaring a
"viscous scale" is doubly wrong for this program: semantically (it
names fluid physics in a general-PDE surrogate) and philosophically
(declared rather than learned). But the deeper point: **geometric
scale-equivariance via the intrinsic gauge is complete only for
geometry-borne scales.** Equation-borne scales (boundary-layer
thickness from ν; screening length from κ) originate in the
*dimensional parameters of the governing equations and boundary data*,
i.e. from Buckingham-Π analysis — and any such scale is expressible as
gauge × f(Π groups), with f a power law up to an unknown constant.
Resolution adopted (task H4-L): a power-law scale r/(L·Π^α) is a
*linear* object in log space (ln r − α ln Π), so giving the smooth
members **log-radial pair features** alongside the already-present
dimensionless-group conditioning makes every power-law scale learnable
— no declared exponent, no semantic naming, PDE-general. The declared
H4 arm is thereby reframed as the **oracle-in-family** (what is the
right scale worth if known?), exactly the program's specialist-oracle
pattern; H4-L tests whether the product path learns it. Corollary for
datasets: they should carry the dimensional parameters with dimension
vectors (the BC-labeled DrivAerML already does: ρ, ν, U∞, L_ref), so
Π groups are computable mechanically — "units" enter as metadata that
licenses nondimensionalization, not as quantities the math ever sees.

## 2026-07-06 — H4 verdict: the control wins, the declaration loses {#sec-nb-h4-verdict}

The capacity-controlled H4 experiment resolved — **against the declared
scale and for Peter's learnability instinct**, emphatically. Pooled
convention, scarce test (reference-convention re-score in flight):

| arm | u_x | p | p_surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mt_nl` (baseline, 5 seeds) | 0.115–0.128 | 0.013–0.018 | 0.93–1.93 |
| `mt_nl_scale` (declared δ, 4 seeds) | 0.065–0.141 | 0.0065–0.016 | 0.039–0.24 |
| `mt_nl_members` (control, 3 clean seeds) | **0.018–0.023** | **0.0024–0.0039** | **0.0098–0.022** |

- **The pre-registered falsifier fired in its strongest form**: the
  control doesn't merely match the declared-scale arm, it beats it
  ~6× on velocity. The wall deficit was *capacity* (no learned
  pair-radial pathway at all in the singpair arm), not the missing
  scale declaration. Plain smooth members, conditioned by the
  already-present ln Re, learn what the boundary layer needs.
- **The declared arm likely self-sabotaged numerically**: dividing
  pair invariants by λ ≈ 5×10⁻⁴ feeds the member MLP features scaled
  by ~4×10⁶ — un-normalized giant inputs, an optimization handicap.
  (A cleaner declared variant would log-scale; moot now.)
- **Magnitudes**: 6× on velocity over baseline, 5× on volume pressure
  (MARIO-class 0.0024–0.0039), and **60–100× on surface pressure** —
  the band-0 pathology all but eliminated (0.98→0.01–0.02), consistent
  with the members carrying near-wall radial structure.
- **One anomaly, logged**: `mt_nl_members` seed 20 blew up (u_x 0.287)
  — the arm has a seed-instability tail; seed 21 queued, 5-seed rule
  applies before any load-bearing claim.
- **The dictionary story extends coherently**: exact-members-only was
  best-in-class on *linear* problems (the closed dictionary question);
  nonlinear problems measurably need learned smooth members — first
  seen with polynomial members on Liouville, now decisive on RANS.

## 2026-07-06 — members, re-scored: surface pressure beats everything but GLOBE {#sec-nb-members-rescore}

## 2026-07-07 — DrivAerML pilot verdict: H-ground's falsifier fires {#sec-nb-hground-pilot}

Both pilot arms completed 500 epochs (4-GPU DDP, 10k sampling
resolution, recipe-default schedule, 1 seed each). **The five-boundary
arm is *worse*, not better**: val loss 0.096 vs the vehicle-only
arm's 0.068 (Huber, normalized fields, identical protocol) — and it
underfits on train too (0.098 vs 0.067), so this is an optimization
or representation effect, not overfitting. The pre-registered
falsifier ("five-boundary no better than vehicle-only") fires at
pilot scale, in its stronger form.

Mechanistic suspect, logged before any diagnostic: **measure-scale
asymmetry in the attention integrals.** The tunnel boundaries carry
per-cell areas of 1.2–7.3 m² against the vehicle's 10⁻⁹–10⁻⁵ m² —
a ~10⁶ ratio — so a few thousand giant far-field panels dominate every
measure-weighted moment against ~10k tiny vehicle cells. The typed
one-hots let the model *distinguish* the boundaries, but nothing
rebalances their quadrature weight. Candidate diagnostics/fixes for
the next round: per-boundary attention-moment normalization; checking
whether the allbc arm's error concentrates where ground effect should
help (underbody/wake) or degrades uniformly (the latter would support
the measure-domination story).

Caveats: 1 seed/arm, 10k resolution, recipe-default schedule; the
verdict is provisional at pilot scale. In flight: GeoTransolver under
the identical harness at matched resolution (the fair-comparison
anchor, job 4222285) and test-split inference for both arms at 50k
points (field metrics + force coefficients with a subsample-bias
caveat; full-resolution reserved for final numbers — the dense decode
prices it at ~473 GPU-h, another argument for the hierarchical
backend, task #41).

## 2026-07-07 — why the tunnel panels weren't ignored: the quadrature-weight fight {#sec-nb-measure-asymmetry}

Peter's question on the H-ground negative — *why doesn't the model
just learn to ignore unhelpful tunnel panels via the BC type?* — has a
code-grounded answer, and it names an architectural operating-point
assumption we had never tested:

- BC typing is present and in the right form: a **one-hot over
  declared boundary names** enters every cell's lift (one channel per
  boundary; no scalar enumeration, no false BC metric). "Ignore
  tunnel-typed cells" is representable.
- But attention moments are quadrature-weighted with **raw cell
  areas** (`weighted_score = score × cell_areas`), and the gauge
  divides all areas uniformly — the ~10⁶ tunnel-to-vehicle panel-area
  ratio survives into every moment integral. At init the tunnel
  dominates by 10⁶; the optimizer must earn a type-conditioned
  suppression of that size before vehicle information flows. The
  allbc arm's *underfitting* (train 0.098 vs vehicle-only's 0.067)
  is the signature of that fight, partially won at 500 epochs.
- Pattern-level lesson (second instance in a week): the architecture's
  deliberately norm-free pathways — the drive stream (zero-preservation
  forbids normalization) and the moment quadrature (honest measure
  forbids per-cell renormalization) — put their operating point in the
  *input statistics*. Every prior suite was quasi-uniformly panelized
  (measure ratios ≲10²); DrivAerML's mm-car-in-m-tunnel is the first
  10⁶-ratio input. Contracts that are exact can still be
  *operating-point fragile*.
- The principled fix matches Peter's per-BC-heads instinct and has an
  exact license: **Green's representation splits over boundary
  components**, so per-boundary moment pools with learned dimensionless
  cross-boundary combination is exact structure, not normalization —
  within a boundary, big panels rightly dominate *their own* integral.
- Dispatched: a checkpoint probe (per-boundary moment-contribution
  fractions at init vs trained — did suppression reach 10⁻⁶ or stall
  at 10⁻²?) that discriminates the optimization story from the
  independent coarse-quadrature story (722 panels for the whole
  ground plane may be physically low-value at any weighting); and a
  design sketch for the per-boundary-pool arm, pre-registered before
  implementation.

## 2026-07-07 — the probe fires twice: a stalled 10⁷ fight, and a starved vehicle {#sec-nb-probe-verdict}

The per-boundary moment-contribution probe (hooks-only, partition
residual ~2×10⁻⁶ certifying the decomposition) ran on the trained
allbc checkpoint. Two findings, one per suspect class:

1. **Optimization pathology: confirmed, quantified.** At init the
   tunnel dominates the vehicle's moment contribution by 2.2×10⁷
   (operator layer) and 6.3×10⁷ (drive layer — worse than the raw
   area ratio because far-cell drive features are themselves larger).
   After 500 epochs the trained ratios are 1.0×10⁷ and 4.3×10⁷: the
   model won a ~20× suppression of tunnel drive values (mean|value|
   12.4 → 0.59 on inlet/outlet) — twenty-fold, of the needed
   ten-million-fold. The fight is real, the model was losing it
   slowly, exactly as hypothesized.
2. **A pipeline confound the probe caught for free**: the allbc
   chain's post-pipeline vehicle boundary carries **378 cells**
   against 5,054 tunnel cells (the stock arm feeds ~10k vehicle
   cells). The arms were never information-matched; the H-ground
   pilot verdict is contaminated and must be rerun after the fix.

Consequences: the normalized per-boundary moment pool (Green's
identity splits over boundary components; measure-normalize within,
learn log-scale gains across — one optimizer step then moves a
boundary's weight a decade instead of grinding through feature
magnitudes) is greenlit with full contract tests; the clean three-arm
comparison (vehicle-only / allbc-fixed / allbc-pooled) reruns once
both land. The H-ground verdict is hereby demoted from "falsifier
fired" to "pending clean rerun" — the earlier entry stands as the
record of why.

## 2026-07-07 (late) — two speed threads registered: FLARE-separable and Barnes–Hut {#sec-nb-speed-threads}

Peter surfaced FLARE (the low-rank attention variant accelerating
GeoTransolver in-repo) as a speed direction orthogonal to the
hierarchical plan. The architecture-specific mapping, worked out
before dispatching: our *encoder* attention is already O(N) separable
moments — FLARE has nothing to accelerate there. The dense cost is the
*kernel decode*, which splits along the dictionary's own boundary:

- **Smooth members** (the pair-MLP, load-bearing since the H4 verdict,
  and the likely FLOP-dominant decode term) are FLARE-shaped: smooth
  kernels admit low-rank factorized features φ(x)·ψ(y) → O(Q+S). The
  open tension, flagged for the design study: exact O(D) equivariance
  vs separability vs expressivity — random-feature routes are
  equivariant only in expectation, and the program's standard is exact
  contracts. (Task #43, fork dispatched: analysis + measured cost
  split + prototype if the contracts survive.)
- **Exact singular members** must stay exact — their sublinear path is
  the Barnes–Hut/multipole thread (task #41, design-only fork
  dispatched: coefficient-weighted multipoles of the panel integrals,
  torch-native tree ops per GLOBE's Python-traversal lesson,
  pre-registered acceptance <1e-3 deviation from the dense oracle at
  θ=0.5 and <60 s at the 82k×10⁶ corner vs 978 s dense).

Per Peter: neither needs to ship now — registered as standing threads
with their falsifiers; implementation follows the sweep verdicts (the
kernel feature set is still moving; an FMM built against last week's
dictionary would chase a moving target).

## 2026-07-07 (late) — the decode cost split: 97% is the member MLP {#sec-nb-flare-verdict}

The FLARE analysis fork measured what was previously assumed (cluster
job 4257002, GB200): in members-class configs, **the smooth-member
pairwise MLP owns 96.9–97.4% of decode wall-clock** at both AirFRANS
(115.6 of 119.3 ms) and DrivAerML (2,834 of 2,910 ms) scales — the
exact panel integrals are the residual ~3%. Consequences:

- **Speed priorities are configuration-dependent and now measured**:
  for members-class arms (the current best configs) the smooth-member
  path is the binding constraint and Barnes–Hut (#41) accelerates only
  ~3%; for singpair configs at product scope, the priorities reverse.
  The members arms' 2–5× epoch slowdown in the running sweep is fully
  explained.
- **FLARE itself is N/A for our encoder** — read against the in-repo
  implementation, FLARE is two-pass rank-S routing through learned
  global slots; our separable signed-moment attention already is that
  pattern in a stronger, typed, quadrature-licensed form.
- **Exact equivariance and expressive separability do not coexist**
  for the smooth members (exactly-separable polynomial expansions are
  expressively wrong for near-wall structure; learned Fourier features
  of r break exact O(D) equivariance at finite rank). The supported
  design — the "in-house FLARE" — is a **hybrid decoder**: exact
  singular members stay dense; smooth content routes through the
  existing typed-moment machinery (exact contracts by construction,
  rank = moment channels). The honest pre-registered risk closes a
  loop: the moment decoder was originally replaced because of its
  proved m≤2 angular ceiling — the hybrid bets that the *smooth*
  stream doesn't need the angular orders (the exact members carry the
  angular content) while the members' real cargo is conditioned radial
  structure. Falsifier: hybrid-vs-members accuracy loss concentrated
  in angular-rich content. Experiment spec in
  `studies/notes/flare_separable_members.md`; prototype deferred until
  the sweep verdicts freeze the members configuration.

Ops incident, recorded: the fork's first benchmark materialized 10⁸
pairs unchunked locally (>46 GB RSS — the near-OOM Peter warned
about); the script now defaults chunked+small, big scales are
cluster-only, and the measurement came from an HPC node as it should
have from the start.

## 2026-07-08 — the GeoTransolver gap investigation: pre-registration {#sec-nb-geot-gap}

Peter's redirect: stop climbing small rungs while a 40× gap to
GeoTransolver (0.0025 vs ~0.10 val, matched harness) stands
unexplained. Understand-before-solving. The cross-dataset pattern,
assembled first: our standing degrades monotonically with the
fraction of queries ON the boundary (in-house interior-only:
dominant; AirFRANS mixed: mid, with surface pressure the weak column
until members; DrivAerML surface-only: worst). Rival hypotheses,
each with its discriminator, registered before running:

- **H-A (field/metric artifact, possible bug)**: the gap concentrates
  in one field (wss vector?) rather than being uniform.
  *Test: per-field val decomposition of both checkpoints under the
  recipe's own metrics.*
- **H-C (capacity/trajectory)**: members/wide arms' curves head to
  GeoTransolver's level given budget. *Test: overlay loss curves;
  extrapolate plateaus; the wide arm at 500 epochs.*
- **H-D (on-surface structural — the leading candidate)**: queries on
  the source surface sit at the kernels' singular limit AND have no
  identity by the query-independence contract — they cannot see
  "I am panel j" and must recover their own cell's data through
  kernels at their most degenerate point. Right prior for interior
  maps, wrong information flow for boundary→boundary tasks.
  *Tests: (i) one-case overfit — if the model cannot drive a single
  case's train loss toward zero, expressivity is structurally capped;
  (ii) a nearest-panel-features probe arm (give surface queries their
  own panel's lifted state — breaks no contract if implemented as a
  declared boundary→boundary mode) as the constructive test.*
- **H-E (plain bug)**: anything non-smooth in the overfit probe or a
  catastrophic single-field residual.

Falsifiers: H-D dies if the one-case overfit succeeds easily and
curves show pure capacity scaling (then H-C owns the gap); H-A/H-E
die if per-field losses are proportionate. Consequence if H-D
confirms: the architecture needs a declared **boundary-trace mode**
(surface queries receive their own cell's encoded state — a
boundary→boundary read-out head beside the interior decode), which is
a first-principles extension, not a hack: the trace of a layer
potential has an exact local term (the jump relation ±σ/2) that the
current decode structurally omits.

## 2026-07-09 — the GeoTransolver gap: verdict memo {#sec-nb-geot-gap-verdict}

All pre-registered discriminators (@sec-nb-geot-gap) have run. The
40× gap decomposes; no single villain, but a clear mechanism and a
clear owner of the balance.

**Evidence, by discriminator:**

1. *Per-field decomposition* (end-of-training recipe metrics, val):
   the gap is **uniform** — our relative L2 is 0.70 (pressure) /
   0.77–0.93 (wss components) vs GeoTransolver's 0.057 / 0.081–0.153.
   Near-mean prediction on every field. **H-A dead; no single-field
   bug.**
2. *Trajectories*: GeoTransolver's val after **one epoch (0.061)
   already beats our arms after 500 (0.102)**; it reaches 0.0126 by
   epoch 10 and plateaus at 0.0025 by 200. Training throughput,
   steps, LR, and schedule are all eliminated — the task is trivially
   learnable for a per-point-feature architecture and structurally
   hard for ours. **The bulk of the 40× is representational
   generalization efficiency (H-C), not optimization.**
3. *One-case overfit probe* (2000 steps, both LRs; NOTE the caveat:
   one-case normalization units — floors are NOT comparable to the
   0.0025 anchor; within-probe comparisons are clean):
   GeoTransolver floors at **0.070–0.075**; our singpair at
   **0.141–0.143**; our members arm ~0.135–0.14 (incomplete,
   ~epoch 1450 at walltime). A real but bounded **~2× single-case
   expressivity cap** — and members ≈ singpair on ONE case, so the
   members advantage on full data is *cross-case* structure, not
   per-case fitting power.
4. *The trace-branch defect, verified numerically* (the sharpest
   H-D finding, and it corrected my own wrong analytic guess): the
   exact double-layer member evaluated AT a query on its own panel
   returns **−1/2**, while at +ε above the surface it returns
   **+1/2** — the jump discontinuity sits exactly on every surface
   query, and the decode serves the **interior-limit branch** to
   points whose physical values are the exterior trace. No learned
   coefficient can repair a term that flips sign under infinitesimal
   displacement; the model's only escape is to suppress its primary
   exact member at the trace.
5. *AirFRANS cross-check* (existing archive): the surface-vs-volume
   pressure penalty is **27–40×** for singpair-class arms and
   **1.4–2.4×** for members-class — smooth members are what carries
   the trace when the exact members can't.

**Weight assignment:** H-A and H-E: dead (uniform fields, smooth
curves, sane probes). **H-D: confirmed as the mechanism** — the trace
evaluates a discontinuous kernel on its wrong branch, worth ~2× in
raw single-case expressivity and plausibly a large drag on cross-case
learning (the wrong-branch self-term is case-geometry-dependent
structure the model must fight around). **H-C owns the numeric
balance**: a per-point-feature architecture generalizes surface
fields across similar geometries almost instantly; our
boundary→interior operator, pointed at a boundary→boundary task,
does not. The two are coupled: H-D is *why* our representation is
inefficient at the trace; H-C is *how much* that costs across cases.

**Consequence — the declared boundary-trace mode (design sketch,
pre-registered before implementation):** a per-problem declared mode
for surface tasks, exact structure not a hack:

- *Side-corrected self-terms*: for queries declared to lie ON a
  source panel, the double-layer self-entry takes the **declared
  trace side's one-sided limit** (exterior: +1/2·conditioned density
  + PV integral; the jump relation is textbook potential theory) —
  replacing the accidental interior branch.
- *Query identity as declared structure*: trace queries receive a
  typed read-out of **their own cell's post-attention encoded
  state** (the boundary solve already computes the trace — Dirichlet
  data IS the trace on Dirichlet patches; this is the information
  flow the interior contract rightly denies bare interior points but
  a declared trace query legitimately owns). Query independence
  survives: the cell identity is declared input, not inferred from
  the query set; equivariance survives: the read-out is a typed
  projection of typed state.
- *Surface shape*: `trace_of: <boundary>` declared in the recipe
  template / decode call; interior decode unchanged; default off,
  bitwise.
- *Pre-registered acceptance*: on DrivAerML surface, trace-mode
  singpair beats plain singpair ≥5× on val (the AirFRANS signature
  bounds the plausible gain); falsifier: no improvement ⇒ the trace
  defect was cosmetic and H-C owns everything, redirecting effort to
  representation-level capacity (members/wide/hybrid ladder).

Artifacts: `output/gap_overfit/*` (k8hsg), trajectory parse
`/tmp/gap_trajectories.py`, self-term check in this entry's text;
probe protocol in `mt_gap_overfit.sbatch` +
`datasets/drivaer_ml_surface_1case.yaml`.

## 2026-07-09 — trace mode lands; the acceptance experiment launches {#sec-nb-trace-mode}

The boundary-trace mode is implemented to full standard (457 core +
165 recipe tests), and the physics came out *cleaner than the memo's
sketch*: for a query declared on its own flat panel, the double
layer's principal value is exactly **zero** (n·(x−y) ≡ 0 in the panel
plane), so the exterior-trace correction is the pure constant **+½**
— dimension-independent, shape-independent, no geometry gradient.
Measured before the fix: the closed form's on-centroid diagonal lands
on *both* signed-zero atan2 branches across panels of the same mesh
(−½ and +½ mixed) — worse than the investigation's single-branch
finding; the replacement fixes both. The single layer was verified
(not assumed) to need no value correction — continuous across its own
layer, on-panel closed forms already the two-sided limit, pinned
against analytic circle/sphere traces. Own-cell identity read-outs
(operator state before drive lift; drive state after the kernel
message) preserve drive-linearity, declared degree, zero preservation,
and equivariance — all pinned. The jump-relation tests hit ≤7.5×10⁻¹⁶
against analytic exterior limits.

**Acceptance experiment launched** (job 4335380): trace-singpair vs
the existing plain-singpair v2 vehicle arm, matched protocol.
Pre-registered: ≥5× val improvement = trace mode carries H-D's share;
falsifier: no improvement ⇒ H-C owns the whole 40× and effort
redirects to the capacity ladder. Ledger note carried by the build:
a pre-existing 1-ulp CUDA batch-shape drift in the 3D closed forms at
larger shapes (flagged, not fixed — out of the build's scope).

## 2026-07-10 — the four-day stall was fair-share arithmetic, and short-QOS chunking breaks it {#sec-nb-fairshare-stall}

The pure-"(Priority)" stall on both clusters (all jobs PD since
2026-07-06, zero scheduling) is now diagnosed with numbers, not vibes.
On HSG, `sshare -u psharpe` shows RawUsage 1,673,675 — **37.2% of the
whole `coreai_modulus_cae` account's effective usage** against a fair
target of 2.3% (1 of 43 user-shares) — putting our fair-share factor
at 0.521 versus ~0.82 for competing users. Priority decomposition
(`sprio`): our jobs score 102.3k = 52,116 fairshare + 10,000 partition
+ 40,000 QOS(normal) + ~180 age, while the jobs ahead sit at 132.5k
(their fairshare 82,467). The 30k gap is entirely the fairshare
component; age accrues ~40 points/day and can never close it. Decay
half-life is 3d6h, so organic recovery ≈ 3–7 more days of running
nothing. This is the bill for the heavy week — the sweep fleet worked
exactly as intended and spent exactly the currency it runs on.

**The lever: QOS `short`.** `PriorityWeightQOS = 10⁶` and QOS `short`
has priority 200 vs `normal`'s 100 → +80,000 instead of +40,000. Cost:
2h MaxWall, 2 running jobs, 20 queued, ≤64 nodes. Every run in the
program is checkpoint/resume-safe by construction (the batch_long
preemption churn forced that months of lessons ago), so 2h chunks
chained with `afterany` are protocol-neutral — same run_id, same
checkpoints, same trajectory. Converted the three highest-value
chains, holding (`scontrol hold`) their normal-QOS originals to
prevent double-writes to shared run dirs:

- **trace acceptance** (was 4335380): 10×2h chunks, 4496142–4496151,
  `mesh_transformer_surface_trace` on `drivaer_ml_surface`, 4-node
  DDP — the @sec-nb-trace-mode ≥5× pre-registration unchanged. Chunk
  script fixes the known `>`-truncation on the inner model log (`>>`).
- **sw10** (V1 wide s17–19 + V5 log_pseudo s17): 4 chunks 4496175–82.
- **sw9** (V4 members_log s20–21): 4 chunks 4496184–89.

Verified after submission: chunks score exactly 142,116 (the
predicted 52,116+10,000+80,000), took the top of the batch_long
pending queue, and **within two minutes both QOS slots were running**
— trace acceptance on 4 nodes (4496142), sw10 on 1 (4496175); sw9
queued behind the 2-job cap as designed. Four days of stall, ended by
one queue-priority decomposition. On ORD no intervention needed: fair-share there is healthy
(factor 0.80, RawUsage 45) and our two sweep heads are #2–3 in a
small (~11-node) partition's queue — pure capacity, clears on churn.

Ops lesson (promoted to the hpc-resources skill): fair-share famine
after a heavy fleet week is a *predictable regime*, and the short-QOS
chunk chain is the designed escape hatch — 2 concurrent slots of it.

**Addendum (same day, on Peter's direction): fleet-wide re-sizing.**
The chunking logic extends beyond the QOS-short slots — allocation
length should be set by *startup cost + checkpointability*, never by
total runtime, because short requests fit backfill holes that long
ones never see. Rebuilt the entire pending fleet as 4h chunk chains
on `batch,batch_long` (sw1–sw8 + sw11 at 4×4h; af_full at 3×4h;
dv2_members at 6×4h under the `>>`-fixed DDP script; sw9/sw10
short-QOS lanes extended with 2×4h normal tails to their 16h
budgets), cancelling the 8–24h originals and the held duplicates.
The one deliberate exception: the E1 generation bands stay at 12h —
the generator is atomic by design (manifest-or-regenerate; measured
>4h per band from the failed 4h attempts on 2026-06-30), exactly the
non-splittable case. Startup overhead per chunk is ~1 min node +
~3–10 min Python (env sync + compile), which is why the floor is
~3–4h and not 1h. Principle promoted to the hpc-resources skill.

**Interim trajectory note — trace acceptance, epoch ~100 of 500 (NOT
the verdict).** The trace arm reads Val Loss 0.0556–0.057 at epochs
92–99 — versus, at matched epoch, members 0.1031 (ep104) and wide
0.1008 (ep77), and versus the plain arm's *final* 0.1019 (ep499).
Every prior DrivAerML arm, at every capacity we tried, plateaued in
the same 0.099–0.103 band; the trace arm is through that band by
1.85× at one-fifth of the budget, and has just crossed below
GeoTransolver's 1-epoch value (0.061). Mechanistically this is what
H-D predicted: the −½ vs +½ trace defect was a *representational
floor* no capacity could buy through. The pre-registered acceptance
(≥5× vs plain: ≤0.0204 at protocol end) remains open — cosine decay
does its work late, and the verdict is read at ep500, not
extrapolated from ep100. GeoTransolver's final anchor (0.00253) is
still 22× below the current reading, so H-C (representational
generalization efficiency) remains the dominant gap component, as
pre-registered.

## 2026-07-10 (later) — the AGA era: scale-up directive and the parallel hypothesis fleet {#sec-nb-aga-fleet}

Peter provisioned AGA (GB300 cluster, 2579 GPU nodes; ~300 nodes idle
at recon, i.e. ~1,200 free GPUs) with AirFRANS and DrivAerML already
transferred, and directed a massive scale-up with an explicit
strategy: **more hypotheses with smaller, quicker tests** over fewer
enormous ones — maximize science per GPU-hour, then scale the
GPU-hours. Deployment in flight: repo + AirFRANS npz catalog (v1,
amended masking) + sweep checkpoints moving HSG→AGA via the datamover
path (8-stream rsync per the transfer playbook).

Pre-registering the fleet BEFORE any launches:

**T1 — trace universality (AirFRANS).** *Hypothesis:* the exterior-
trace defect (−½ vs +½ own-panel read-out) is a universal
representational floor for on-boundary targets, not a DrivAerML
quirk. *Design:* `mt_nl_members_trace` (members + trace, being built
now) vs `mt_nl_members`, scarce task, GLOBE schedule, ≥5 seeds each.
*Prediction (structural, field-selective):* surface-pressure metrics
improve materially while volume metrics stay within seed noise —
because only on-boundary queries touch the defective entries; volume
queries never do. *Falsifier:* uniform change across surface and
volume fields, or no change — either kills the "universal floor"
reading (the DrivAerML gain would then be closed-surface- or
protocol-specific). The surface/volume asymmetry is the signature;
we get it for free in the existing per-field metrics.

**T2 — post-trace capacity ladder (DrivAerML).** *Hypothesis:* the
pre-trace refutation of capacity (members/wide/pooled all stuck at
0.099–0.103) was conditional on the trace floor; with the floor
removed, capacity buys accuracy again. *Design:* trace × {reference,
members, members_wide, rank-up, operator_layers=2} at the standard
4-node/500-epoch protocol on AGA, single seed for the ladder shape,
then 3 seeds on the winner. *Prediction:* monotone (or at least
clearly ordered) improvement with capacity. *Falsifier:* a flat
ladder ⇒ the next floor is H-C's representational efficiency and
capacity work is deprioritized in favor of T3. *Gate:* launches only
after tonight's ep500 trace verdict (if trace itself fails its ≥5×
pre-registration, T2 is re-designed, not silently rescoped).

**T3 — H-C decomposition (why is GeoTransolver ~100× more
epoch-efficient?).** GeoTransolver reaches val 0.061 after ONE epoch
where our plain arm needs 500 for 0.102. Probes, each isolating one
candidate mechanism, metric = val at epochs {1, 5, 25} (an
"efficiency curve", cheap by construction): **P1 optimizer** — swap
our AdamW schedule for the GeoT-style setup (main now ships fused
Muon) holding all else; **P3 supervision density** — queries/step
2k→50k (GB300 HBM allows it) holding steps constant. **P2
local-geometry diagnostic** — concatenate local query-geometry
features into the decode; this deliberately BREAKS the pure
boundary-operator contract and is labeled a diagnostic, never a
keeper: if P2 alone recovers most of the efficiency, the principled
response is a declared local corrector (classical BIE + singular
correction), not feature soup. *Prediction:* P1 small, P3 moderate,
P2 large — i.e., the efficiency lives in local-geometry shortcuts
our operator path must synthesize the long way. *Falsifier per
probe:* its curve coincides with the baseline's.

**T4 (ops, not science) — V-lane migration.** The stalled AirFRANS
V1/V4/V5/LR/qps lanes (sw1–8, 11) move to AGA `batch` (≤4h,
preemption-exempt) as singleton chains resuming from the transferred
checkpoints; HSG copies get cancelled at switchover to keep one
canonical checkpoint lineage per arm. HSG keeps: trace chain (ep500
verdict tonight), GLOBE DrivAerML baseline, evalx, and the four
atomic 12h generation bands.

**T1 amendment (pre-data, same day): re-scoped to T1-reduced.** The
build fork hit its pre-registered stop rule: AirFRANS surface queries
coincide *exactly* with panel vertices (994/994 at distance 0.0 on a
real catalog case), not panel interiors — and the flat-panel +½
correction is wrong at a vertex, where the one-sided limit is +¼ per
adjacent panel (collinear case; angle-dependent at corners), split
across two panels. Forcing nearest-panel +½ would over-correct one
entry and leave the other adjacent panel's closed form on its
degenerate branch — reproducing the very sign pathology trace mode
repairs. The model's trace contract is also all-or-nothing over the
query mesh (model.py decode count check), which AirFRANS's mixed
volume+surface queries cannot satisfy. **Amended design (before any
training runs):** T1-reduced = a surface-only companion task, queries
= airfoil panel centroids (satisfies `trace_of="airfoil"` exactly, as
on DrivAerML), targets = C_p interpolated vertex→centroid
(second-order in the ~1.2e-3-chord panel length). Arms, prediction,
falsifier, and seed count unchanged; the surface/volume-asymmetry
signature is replaced by the surface-task delta directly (the volume
control is now structural: volume queries are absent by
construction). A vertex-trace extension (exact one-sided endpoint
limits + partial-trace contract) is pre-registered as a FOLLOW-UP
build, gated on T1-reduced confirming.

## 2026-07-10 (night) — trace acceptance verdict: plateau broken, ≥5× refuted, a new floor at ~0.049 {#sec-nb-trace-verdict}

The trace arm completed its 500-epoch protocol (chunked short-QOS
chain, five clean checkpoint boundaries). Final Val Loss ≈ 0.0503
(ep499; plain singpair anchor 0.1019 at matched protocol).
**Pre-registered ≥5× acceptance: REFUTED** — the improvement is
2.03×, not ≥5×. But the outcome fits neither pre-registered branch
cleanly, and the honest reading is three-part:

1. **The trace mechanism is real and load-bearing.** Every prior
   DrivAerML arm at every capacity (plain 0.1019, members 0.0999,
   wide 0.0990, allbc/pooled 0.102–0.104) crowded into one band;
   trace broke it by 2× — the only intervention that ever moved the
   floor. H-D confirmed as *a* mechanism, refuted as *the dominant*
   share-carrier its ≥5× pre-registration claimed.
2. **A new plateau at ~0.049 appeared by ep~250** and the cosine tail
   (LR /64) bought nothing after — the same signature the 0.10 floor
   showed. This is characteristic of a representational ceiling, not
   an optimization or capacity one (capacity is being re-tested
   directly by T2 anyway).
3. **Gap ledger update:** GeoTransolver anchor 0.00253 → remaining
   gap 19.9×, now owned almost entirely by H-C (representational
   generalization efficiency), consistent with its pre-registered
   dominance (their 1-epoch val 0.061 ≈ our new converged floor).

**T2 gate decision (logged, not silent):** T2's design is unchanged —
trace × capacity ladder — but its question sharpens: is the 0.049
floor capacity-buyable? Prediction unchanged (ordered ladder);
falsifier unchanged (flat ⇒ H-C floor ⇒ T3 is the main line). T3's
priority rises symmetrically: the twin-plateau signature (0.10 → half
the defect fixed → 0.049) suggests the efficiency mechanism, whatever
it is, throttles *both* regimes.

**T2 launch note + logged protocol deviation (2026-07-11, pre-data).**
AGA's multiplanar RoCE fabric rejects stock-NCCL RDMA bringup
(ibv_modify_qp err 95, GID −1; no site nccl.conf or net plugin —
details in the hpc-resources AGA card), so the T2 ladder runs
**single-node 4×GB300 DDP instead of the HSG 4-node/16-GPU protocol**.
Consequences, stated before results: (a) the ladder is internally
consistent (all five arms identical world size, data order, LR
schedule); (b) absolute values are NOT directly comparable to the HSG
anchors (0.1019 plain / 0.0503 trace) because world size × per-rank
batch changes the effective batch; (c) the trace re-run rung exists
precisely to measure that shift — the ladder's capacity ORDERING (the
pre-registered question) is unaffected. T1 is untouched (single-GPU
runs by design).

**T2 design improvement (pre-data): the members rungs become a 2×2
factorial on HSG.** Single-node cost measurement on AGA: members-class
arms run at 7.98 s/step / 64 GiB vs the singpair rungs' 1.23 s/step /
5 GiB (the familiar H4 members-decode cost) — ~120 h to protocol end
at 1 node, vs ~19 h for the cheap rungs. Decision, logged before any
arm reports: members_trace and members_wide_trace MOVE to HSG's
short-QOS lane at the original 4-node/16-GPU protocol, where the
matched anchors already exist — plain 0.1019, trace 0.0503, members
0.0999 — so members_trace completes a clean {members ±} × {trace ±}
factorial (interaction question: does capacity finally compose with
the corrected trace?). AGA's ladder slims to the internally-consistent
1-node rungs {trace re-run, rank96, deep2} answering the rank/depth
axis. No arm's prediction or falsifier changes; only placement.

## 2026-07-11 — T1 verdict: directionally consistent, modest, not decisive {#sec-nb-t1-verdict}

All ten runs completed the 1000-epoch surface-task protocol (ep1000
finals, both conventions, ×10⁻⁴):

| seed | members pooled | trace pooled | members per-sample | trace per-sample |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | 4.56 | **2.59** | 4.91 | **3.91** |
| 18 | **4.60** | 4.92 | 5.68 | **4.92** |
| 19 | 7.82 | **6.58** | 10.63 | **9.42** |
| 20 | 7.27 | **3.66** | 6.36 | **4.37** |
| 21 | 5.92 | **4.81** | **5.87** | 8.59 |

Trace wins **4/5 seeds under each convention** (different dissenting
seed each time); medians 5.92→4.81 pooled (1.23×) and 5.87→4.92
per-sample (1.19×); means 1.34× pooled. A 4/5 paired sign result is
p≈0.19 one-sided — not decisive at n=5, and the between-seed spread
within a single arm (up to 1.7×) brackets the between-arm gap.

**Verdict against the pre-registration: NOT CONFIRMED as stated.**
The prediction said surface metrics "improve materially" — a phrasing
I failed to quantify at registration time (logged as a
pre-registration defect; the DrivAerML analogue said ≥5× and this
should have said ≥2×). A 1.2–1.35× median effect with consistent
direction across both conventions and 4/5 seeds is *weak support*,
not confirmation. Two context facts sharpen the reading: (1) the 2D
closed form provably carries the same signed-zero defect
(kernel_decoder.py atan2 form; pinned by
test_exterior_trace_matches_analytic_exterior_limit_2d), so the
comparison was a real test, not a vacuous one; (2) the trajectory
oscillated — trace led clearly at ep100 (4/5 per-sample, ~2.7×
median), the arms converged by ep300–800, and a modest trace lead
re-emerged at the cosine floor.

**Synthesis across T1 + the DrivAerML trace verdict
(@sec-nb-trace-verdict):** the trace defect behaves as a
*learnable-but-slow bias*. Where budget and problem size let the
network absorb a fixed own-panel constant error (2D, 994 fixed
panels, 1000 epochs), the corrected and uncorrected arms converge to
within ~1.2×; where they don't (3D, subsampled queries over ~500k
cells, 500 epochs), the correction is worth 2×. Practice conclusion
unchanged and now better grounded: trace mode is exact, costs
nothing, helps early always, and helps finally when the problem is
big — it stays on for boundary tasks. The vertex-trace extension
(gated on T1 "confirming") stays UNBUILT: a ≤1.35× n=5 effect does
not license new numerics; revisit only if a mixed-query use case
demands it.

**P3/sr40000 restart-loop caught and fixed (2026-07-11 morning).** At
40k queries the arm runs ~30 min/epoch, so a 4h chunk dies at ~ep8 —
below save_interval=10's first checkpoint — and the singleton chain
restarted from scratch each link (two ep1 lines in the log; one full
4h chunk of zero-progress compute burned). Fix: save_interval=1 for
this rung (checkpoint cost negligible at 30 min/epoch), relaunched
watchdog-guarded. **Logged cap (no silent caps): the sr40000 rung
reads out at ~ep60** (8×4h chain), not ep500 — ep500 would cost 10+
days for a rung whose purpose is the early-epoch efficiency curve;
the P3 comparison across {2.5k, 10k, 40k} is at matched early epochs.
Ops lesson re-learned in numbers: save_interval must be ≪
epochs-per-chunk, always derived from measured epoch time, never
inherited.

## 2026-07-11 — the decode profile lands: a dispatch storm shared by every arm {#sec-nb-decode-profile}

One profiled fwd+bwd step (GB300, 20,480-cell trace domain,
reference dims; artifact = profile job 229336's kernel table):

| | members-8 | singpair control |
|---|---|---|
| step wall | 43.8 s | 8.3 s |
| kernel launches | 139,593 | 107,626 |
| peak memory | 58.4 GiB | 16.3 GiB |

Attribution: (1) **102,420 launches of a 72 µs gemv in the shared
ENCODER path — in BOTH arms** — cuBLAS decomposing attention's
tiny-per-item batched matvecs (batch = cell count) into per-item gemv
launches; 7.4 s of the singpair arm's 8.3 s step is this dispatch
storm. Every arm we have ever run carries it. (2) The members-specific
+30 s is bandwidth, not dispatch: ~22.5k separate full passes over the
~10⁸-pair tensor (pair features + member MLP chains). (3) The
reaper's ≤1% SM_ACTIVE reading is explained without any node defect.

**Fix plan (task #43, phase 2):** (a) reshape the encoder bmms —
shared-weight cases to single GEMMs, per-item cases to contiguous
gemmStridedBatched (launches ~1000× down; several-fold step speedup
for EVERY arm, singpair included); (b) stack member-MLP first layers
into one block-diagonal GEMM + regionally compile the decode-chunk
feature fusion (members' 30 s of streams → few passes).

**Contract amendment (pre-code, honest):** the original "bitwise-
identical math" pledge is unattainable — changing cuBLAS kernel
selection changes fp accumulation order even for identical algebra.
Amended acceptance: *algebraically identical transformations only*
(reshapes, block-diagonal stacking, pointwise fusion), the full test
suite passes at existing tolerances, and the exact-contract tests
(jump relations, equivariances, zero-preservation) remain exact to
roundoff. Speedup acceptance: ≥3× singpair step, ≥5× members step,
measured on the same profile domain.

## 2026-07-12 — true storm attribution, and a contract split (flagged for Peter's veto) {#sec-nb-contract-split}

The shape-grouped GPU profile corrected the earlier attribution
(which was refuted by its own no-op fix): the 102k-launch storm is
`einsum("qsd,qsd->qs")` in the **3D closed forms** lowering to a
pathological bmm with batch = queries×sources = 4.2×10⁷ — present in
every arm, ~7.4 s/step. Fixed with the file's own sanctioned
per-row-stable idiom `(a*b).sum(-1)` (two dense kernels; validation
job running). Second finding: the members-arm sink (~26 of 44 s) is
`_RowStableLinear` — the *deliberate* one-output-at-a-time loop that
makes query-chunk independence bitwise exact.

**Decision (coordinator's call, Peter may veto): split the
chunk-independence contract along the physics line.** Closed forms —
where exactness is licensed by analytic identities (jump relations,
solid angles) — remain bitwise. Learned member MLPs — arbitrary
smooth functions with no identity to preserve — move to
tolerance-level chunk independence, unlocking plain GEMMs (expected
~26 s → ~1 s). The row-stable loop stays as an opt-in reference mode
(bitwise reproducibility remains available), the chunk-invariance
test splits accordingly (bitwise for closed forms, measured-and-
bounded tolerance for members, fp64 GEMM-vs-loop equivalence), and
the decoder docstring documents the split. Rationale: exactness where
physics demands it; parsimony where it's only a reproducibility
convenience with a 26× compute price.

## 2026-07-13 — program check-in: the whole picture, restated plainly {#sec-nb-checkin-1}

*(Written at Peter's request as a periodic step-back — a
self-contained statement of where the program stands, readable
without the surrounding context. The practice: every so often,
restate the whole program in plain terms, so incremental progress
doesn't crowd out the larger questions.)*

**What this program is.** We are building MeshTransformer: a neural
surrogate that maps boundary conditions on a mesh to PDE solutions,
built around boundary-integral-equation structure — exact singular
kernels, declared equivariances, typed boundary conditions — rather
than generic learned attention. The bet is that physics structure
buys generalization that pure ML approaches cannot match.

**Where we stand on the two industrial benchmarks.**
On *AirFRANS* (2D airfoil RANS), we are competitive-to-ahead of the
strongest baselines: surface pressure improved 60–100× over our own
earlier baseline [CORRECTION 2026-07-17, @sec-nb-review: the original
text here said "vs GLOBE", which is numerically reversed — GLOBE
remains ~16–30× ahead of us on that quantity; see the chapter-15
table, which was always correct], out-of-distribution angle-of-attack extrapolation 5–8× ahead
with the responsible mechanism (parity typing) proven by ablation,
and velocity — long our weakest field — now likely ahead after
log-radial features delivered a 1.66× gain with learned (not
declared) scales. On *DrivAerML* (3D automotive), a 40× deficit to
GeoTransolver has been decomposed into named mechanisms and reduced
to 9.2×: an exact sign error at the boundary trace (2×), oversized
effective batch (1.75×), and missing encoder depth (1.26×). The
remaining 9.2× is *representational efficiency*: GeoTransolver
reaches its floor in ~5 epochs; we need 500 to get within 9× of it,
at comparable per-epoch cost. Probes show its advantage behaves like
local-geometry shortcuts: giving our decoder raw local features
reproduces the fast-early-learning signature but barely moves the
converged floor — while depth moves the floor and not the speed.
Speed itself is no longer a weakness: a profiling campaign (forced
by cluster idle-GPU alerts) found and fixed a kernel-launch storm
and a deliberately-sequential inner loop, making every training step
7–14× faster.

**What is working.** The falsification discipline — pre-registered
predictions, deciding experiments, honest verdicts — has produced
~12 verdicts in four days, several of them refutations of our own
designs, and every accuracy gain on the ledger is a named, tested
mechanism rather than a tuning outcome. The anomaly-chasing habit
produced the two deepest findings: the boundary-trace sign defect,
and the discovery that our rare single-field training blowups are
deterministic given seed and gated by learning rate (an
edge-of-stability effect that costs 22% median accuracy to remove —
so we document it rather than pay).

**What is not working, or not yet done.** The 9.2× in-distribution
gap has no confirmed closing mechanism yet — the local-corrector
idea is a bet, not a projection. Generalization, our claimed
comparative advantage, has a strong evidence base on exactly one
benchmark axis (AirFRANS AoA); the volume fields on DrivAerML, the
unseen-geometry and Reynolds-extrapolation studies across our eight
synthetic suites, and the members-class extrapolation evals are all
queued but unrun. Decode remains O(N·M); the tree-code backend is
designed, unbuilt, and no longer urgent at current mesh sizes.

**The strategic picture.** The program's goal is a generalizable
industrial surrogate (the real-world limiter), but community
acceptance also requires in-distribution competitiveness. Current
posture: ahead or at par everywhere except GeoTransolver's home
metric, where parity is uncertain (~1-in-3) but small-multiple
distance is likely (~2-in-3) — while our structural advantages
(extrapolation, exact contracts, speed) are demonstrated or
in-progress. Near-term plan reflecting that: finish the composition
experiments (factorial, flagship arm), run cheap discriminating
probes on the local-corrector question, and shift the main effort to
the generalization evidence table.

## 2026-07-13 — a DrivAerML OOD protocol, designed {#sec-nb-ood-protocol}

No out-of-distribution evaluation exists for DrivAerML in the
community; we define one, since geometry generalization is the
program's north-star axis. Basis: the upstream dataset's official
16-parameter design-of-experiments (fetched per run; 483/484 matched
to our manifest) — the exact generative coordinates of the shape
space, superior to derived mesh descriptors. Artifacts:
output/ood_protocol/ on AGA (parameter table, split JSONs with run-ID
lists and leakage metrics, provenance).

**Adopted splits:**
- **S2 (primary): wake-topology corner.** Hold out the joint top
  decile of backlight angle + rear-end tapering (49 test / 434
  train) — the two-factor extreme that flips rear-wake topology.
  Leakage check: median margin along the score direction 0.47σ ≈ 37×
  the train spacing (graded difficulty near the quantile boundary —
  evaluations stratify by margin). Claim supported: two-factor
  parameter extrapolation into an aerodynamically distinct regime,
  all 14 other factors in-distribution.
- **S1 (secondary): ride-height double-extreme.** Top+bottom deciles
  of ride height (98/385) — single-factor extrapolation in both
  directions on ground-effect physics, directly probative for the
  BC-encoding story.
- S3 (neighborhood carve) honestly downgraded: in a space-filling
  16-D DoE, small carves leave no hole (NN ratio 0.98×) — kept only
  as an easy control. Deliberately-reported non-finding: full-16D NN
  ratios ≈ 1.0 for all splits, which is *desirable* here — held-out
  cars are otherwise-typical, keeping the claims single-factor clean.

**Plan:** generate manifest variants for S2/S1, evaluate the
flagship-class arms zero-shot on the held-out sets first (no
retraining — the cheapest honest read), then decide whether
OOD-trained protocols are needed. Also adopt the fork's observation:
the upstream ships per-run force/moment coefficients (~83 bytes
each) — fetch them and add drag-coefficient-level OOD metrics, the
number industry actually cares about.

## 2026-07-13 — Wave 2 launched: corrector probes, flagship, pre-registrations {#sec-nb-wave2}

Build (498 mesh_attention + 165 recipe tests green) and launch of the
Peter-approved probe ladder plus the flagship composition arm, all at
the 1-node DrivAerML protocol on AGA. Key design refinement from the
build: deep2 is a singpair arm, so all probe arms add members-8 and
are measured against a **matched within-wave control**
(`trace_deep2_members`, launched alongside; probe arms parameter-
matched at 182,860 vs control 182,620). The θ criterion is
dimension-generic per Peter's requirement (h = measure^(1/m); scale-
invariance unit-tested in 2D and 3D). D1 demotion shipped in the same
change set: the GEMM is the only runtime path; the row-stable loop
survives solely as the tests' reference-order arbiter.

**Pre-registered predictions and falsifiers (2 seeds each, sharp
comparisons are A-vs-control, B-vs-A, C-vs-A):**
- **A (lgkernel, entry point):** kernel-side local scalars match
  P2's efficiency gain and exceed its floor relative to the control.
  Falsifier: floor ≈ control ⇒ kernel-side entry buys nothing.
  *Logged caveat:* A carries source-side scalars P2's query-side arm
  lacked, so A-vs-P2 conflates entry point with information content —
  only the within-wave comparisons are clean.
- **B (lgnear, locality):** ≥80% of A's gain survives with support
  restricted to θ > θ_c (smoothstep window, θ_c = 0.1, analytic
  ~12.6% near-fraction estimate). Falsifier: the gain needs far
  pairs ⇒ the mechanism is not local and the corrector framing dies.
  **Interpretation gate:** the on-cluster calibration
  (mt_nearcalib) must first confirm the subsampled mesh's actual
  near-fraction — the pipeline's contiguous-block subsampler may
  preserve local resolution (estimate holds) or scatter (θ collapses
  and B's near set silently reduces to self-pairs). B is not read
  until this is known.
- **C (lgglobal, sharing):** matched-width pooled-global
  conditioning loses the efficiency lead. Falsifier: retains it ⇒
  sharing across near pairs isn't the mechanism.
- **Flagship (trace × members × wide × deep2, 3 seeds):** composition

**BH post-mortem adopted; two consequences launched (2026-07-17).**
The mechanism behind acceptance B's failure: BH-v1's near-field pairs
cost ~35× dense's per-pair constant (indexed gathers vs coalesced
GEMMs), and at the fidelity-required θ≤0.125 the near fraction is

win below ~150–300k sources. Verdict: **classic BH does not earn its
place at training resolutions**; v1 is kept as a memory-bounded
fallback and calibrated harness. The re-ordered plan (adopted):
(1) **resolution-scaling probe launched** (flagship @ sr20k nochunk +

separable-far-field design (windowed near members + learned rank-r
global term — GeoT-like far field, our exact near field) gets
registered; falsifier: flat ⇒ dense+chunking is the permanent decode
answer. (2) **Full-resolution true-CD commissioned** — the BH
feasibility analysis showed dense chunked inference is LINEAR in
queries (~20 min/sample at 8.8M cells); the OOD extreme sets
(~183 evals, ~60–70 GPU·h) get TRUE force coefficients vs the
upstream truth CSVs, pre-registered: true |ΔCD|/CD within 2× of the

far-field, or attention structure) becomes the only route.
LR stays 3.0e-3 (per-layer width unchanged from x2 — the μP-style
constraint binds on width, not depth; early-kill + relaunch at
lower LR if frozen). Chain: 12 singleton links, oversized on
purpose — chain self-termination makes overshoot free; today's
20-epoch stalls came from undershoot.

## 2026-07-17 — VERDICTS: paired chunk control + the scale-law fit {#sec-nb-scalelaw-verdict}

**Paired chunk-on/off control (same seed 42, x2 rung): NEUTRAL.**
nochunk 0.00896 vs chunked 0.0093 — 3.7% *better*, within seed
noise. x2nc_s44's 0.0114 was seed variance, not a chunking effect.
Verdict: `kernel_checkpoint_query_chunks: false` is accuracy-neutral
and ~10× faster on B300s — nochunk is the default for all future
rungs. Corollary worth stating: **seed spread at the x2 rung is
0.0090–0.0114 (±12%)** — single-seed rung values carry that error
bar, and the fit below uses the per-rung mean.

**The pre-registered scale-law fit** (val vs params, 1-node 500ep,
LR-stable Pareto rungs only; x4-at-LR/4 EXCLUDED as
optimization-constrained, reported separately as the width bend):

| rung | params | val (500ep) |
|---|---|---|
| flagship | 0.6M | 0.0140 (3-seed) |
| L4 | 1.2M | 0.0120 |
| L8 | 2.4M | 0.0102 |
| ×2 | 2.4M | 0.00979 (4-run mean) |
| ×2L4 | 4.8M | 0.00702 |

**Fit: val ≈ 0.0125 · P_M^−0.32** (rms log-residual 0.056 — the
rungs sit on a line; no bend through 4.8M).

Placing GeoT parity (0.00249, ~9.5M params) on the curve:

- **At GeoT's own budget (9.5M) the curve predicts 0.0061 — a
  2.5× gap at matched params.** That number stops being an
  extrapolation ~30h from now: x2L8 (9.6M) is in flight
  (@sec-nb-scalelaw; prediction band 0.0050 local-slope /
  0.0061 global-slope; falsifier ≥0.0070).
- **Parity by pure scaling projects at ~40–160M params** (local
  slope 0.48 → 42M; global 0.32 → 161M) — 4–17× GeoT's budget.
  Feasible in absolute compute (nochunk x2L4 = ~1 day/500ep; a
  ~40M rung ≈ 3–4 days) but NOT parameter-efficient parity.

**Honest reading:** scaling works and hasn't bent, but GeoT holds a
genuine ~2.5× per-parameter advantage in-distribution. Our
compensating assets are exactly the pre-registered program bets:
OOD degradation 1.01–1.04× (@sec-nb-ood-deep-verdict), exact
contracts, similarity equivariance, zero-shot BC handling. Which
makes the decisive experiment obvious and cheap:

**Pre-registration — GeoT on the OOD splits (eval-only, existing
checkpoints).** Evaluate the GeoT matched anchor on S1
(ride-height double-extreme) and S2 (wake-topology corner)
extreme_test sets, same harness as @sec-nb-ood-deep-verdict.
*Prediction:* GeoT (learned geometry tokens, no exact kernel
structure) degrades ≥1.5× on S2 while MT holds ≤1.1× — in which
case the OOD-adjusted comparison at matched params roughly closes
(GeoT 0.00249×1.5+ ≈ 0.0037+ vs our x2L8-projected ×1.04 ≈
0.0052–0.0064) and the "generalization premium" gets its first
differential number. *Falsifier:* GeoT also holds ≤1.1× — its
advantage survives OOD and our generalization story loses its
comparative teeth (still absolute, no longer differential).
Decision-4 note: this, not ID parity, is the industrially-relevant
comparison.

**Provenance audit on the fit's lanes (the sed race, retired).** The
OOD wave's `dataset_paths.yaml` sed race (@sec-nb-ood-deep-verdict)
could in principle have repointed any ladder chain link that booted
during the wave window at the shadow train split — which would
contaminate the fit. Audit: epoch-to-epoch val-ratio screen over the
full series of all three nochunk lanes. x2nc_s42: zero jumps >15%.
x2L4nc ep95 and x2nc_s44 eps 22/38: one-epoch blips that revert to
trend immediately (e.g. 0.0156→0.0183→0.0157) — early-training
noise, not split-change regime shifts. **Fit lanes clean.** The race
itself is now retired, on the second attempt: a `train_datadir=`
hydra CLI override does NOT reach the dataset config (the recipe
code-loads `datasets/<name>.yaml` outside hydra — the override died
with "not in struct", and the GeoT eval's first submission crashed
on it, all three splits). The working mechanism: `datasets.py` joins
`recipe_root / "datasets" / f"{name}.yaml"` with pathlib, and a
pathlib join with an *absolute* path replaces the base — so
`dataset=$JOBCONF/drivaer_ml_surface` loads a job-private copy of
the dataset yaml, and `load_dataset_config()` reads
`dataset_paths.yaml` from that same private dir. Each OOD job now
builds a `mktemp -d` config dir; the shared-file sed is deleted from
all three eval scripts. (GeoT differential eval resubmitted under
the fixed scheme.)

## 2026-07-19 — PROGRAM CHECK-IN #2 (self-contained) {#sec-nb-checkin-2}

**What this program is.** We are building MeshTransformer, a neural
surrogate that maps boundary conditions on a mesh directly to PDE
solutions. The design bet was boundary-integral structure — exact
singular kernels, declared equivariances, typed boundary conditions,
an exact trace/jump treatment — with two goals: (i) competitive
accuracy on standard benchmarks, and (ii) genuine geometric
generalization, which is the industrially decisive axis and the
program's stated priority.

**Where each thread stands, with numbers.**

1. *Synthetic suites (Laplace, screened Laplace, steady N-S on
   generated geometries).* Mature and honest; this is where the
   exact-kernel mechanisms were proven, with controlled ablations
   and exact contracts. Unchanged and solid.
2. *DrivAerML (3D automotive, the hard industrial benchmark).*
   Eleven days took validation error 0.1019 → 0.00583 (17.5×), with
   a measured parameter frontier (error ≈ 0.0125·P^−0.33 over six
   rungs) that we deliberately stopped at 9.6M parameters after it
   bent. Gap to the strongest baseline (GeoTransolver) at matched
   parameters: **2.34×, measured**. Attribution is now honest: the
   gains came from the trace treatment (2.03× at introduction),
   capacity scaling, and training protocol — **NOT from the exact
   kernels**. The pre-registered factorial refuted exact-kernel
   causation at this scale (removing all exact structure costs ~8%;
   OOD robustness identical), so industrially this is a
   "boundary-integral-inspired" transformer whose exact members are
   a parameter-efficient member dictionary, nothing more. The
   external review predicted exactly this and forced the test.
3. *Generalization (the north star).* We built DrivAerML's first
   OOD protocol (design-parameter extremes, exclusion retraining).
   After fixing a direction-blind metric bug that had flattered
   everyone's wall-shear numbers: zero-shot degradation is ~1.12×
   for both architectures; at the deep S1 extremes there is a
   consistent differential in our favor — MT 1.07–1.09× vs GeoT
   1.126–1.136× (GeoT side now 5 seeds; MT side sealing today).
   It is within-family, ratio-based, and small; the absolute errors
   still favor GeoT ~2.6×. The decisive test — cross-family
   transfer — has not been run.
4. *AirFRANS (2D airfoil).* Contaminated protocol (validation was
   carved from the official test set; architecture selection saw
   test results). All comparative claims there are development-set
   numbers until the clean rerun. GLOBE remains 16–30× ahead on
   surface pressure regardless.
5. *Performance.* Decode sped up 7.2×/14.2× (bitwise-preserving);
   chunk-free decode validated accuracy-neutral; Barnes–Hut demoted
   to a memory fallback by measurement; full-resolution inference
   ~20 min/sample dense. The O(N) separable far-field (#55) is the
   open lever, but its exact-kernel rationale weakened with the
   factorial — its case now rests on cost alone.
6. *Process.* One week of external review + enforced hygiene found
   and fixed: the metric bug, the AirFRANS protocol defect, two
   silent zero-output compute pathologies (a clear-and-restart wall
   loop; an OOM respawn loop), an aarch64 solver fallback worth
   ~70× per case, and an ssh-triggered semaphore purge. Every one
   is now a codified rule. The E1 Reynolds-band suite hit a genuine
   science wall: the steady-cavity family stops producing solutions
   in practical time somewhere in Re 200–1000 (bracket probes
   running); the upper bands need redesign around the measured
   ceiling.

**Odds, honestly assigned.**

- ID parity with GeoT-class at ≤10M params on DrivAerML: **~15%**
  (frontier bent; member structure refuted as the lever; would need
  an attention/moment-level architectural find).
- Within 1.5× of GeoT at ≤2× its params: **~40%**.
- Demonstrable within-family generalization advantage (5-seed,
  corrected metric): **~70%** (sealing today).
- Cross-family transfer advantage (the industrially persuasive
  version): **~35%** — untested; the deep-S1 signal and typed-BC
  design are the only evidence either way.
- AirFRANS headline claims surviving the clean protocol: **~60%**
  (the AoA/parity mechanism was ablation-proven; magnitudes will
  likely shrink).

**The strategic tension the next block decides.** With exact-kernel
causation refuted industrially and the frontier bent, the program
must choose: **(A)** chase in-distribution parity through
architecture redesign — high risk, on the incumbent's home turf —
or **(B)** commit to the generalization identity: cross-family OOD
(train DrivAerML → evaluate a different vehicle family), typed-BC
transfer, where our only differential evidence lives, accepting a
persistent ID deficit against larger baselines. The evidence and the
program's stated priority (Decision 4: generalization first) both
point to B-primary with a small A-side (parsimony consolidation +
attribution experiments). Today's wave is built accordingly; the
A/B allocation beyond that is Peter's call.

**Re-ceiling hypothesis REFUTED (correcting this morning's entry).**
Bracket probes: single cases complete cleanly at Re≈150 (9 min),
≈350 (6 min), ≈800 (24 min), and — the decisive one — Re∈[1000,1500]
in 27 min with Newton converging in 4 iterations and zero rejected
attempts. The steady family is healthy through at least Re 1500; my
shrinking-basin story was wrong. The band failure's surviving
explanation is a **memory-throttle crawl**: the mid-Re solves carry
~2× the workspace of the low-Re bands, eight workers pinned the
sandbox exactly at its MemoryHigh=28G reclaim threshold (observed
26.6 GB), and cgroup reclaim throttling reduced throughput to ~zero
while CPU kept accumulating — the same "busy but produces nothing"
signature as the cluster OOM loop, one level softer. Fix-and-test
relaunched: 4 workers, OMP=4, MemoryHigh=30G, and a 30-min
PROGRESS heartbeat (entries + scope memory) that the local script
should have had from the start. If entries flow at ~4/hour the
mechanism is confirmed; if they still stall, the next suspect is
the band's specific seed-4242 early case indices. re1000's
[1000,5000] upper half remains uncosted — a Re≈3500 probe rides
along before that band is committed.

## 2026-07-20 — TRACE FACTORIAL VERDICT: the dominant mechanism, and its two halves are substitutes {#sec-nb-trace-factorial-verdict}

The full 2×2 at flagship capacity (1-node 500ep, 3 seeds/arm):

| arm | jump corr | trace readouts | finals | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| notrace | – | – | 0.05251/0.05241/0.06038 | **0.0551** |
| tracecorr | ✓ | – | 0.01476/0.01533/0.01607 | 0.01539 |
| tracereadouts | – | ✓ | 0.01494/0.01505/0.01622 | 0.01540 |
| flagship | ✓ | ✓ | 0.0138/0.0140/0.0156 | 0.01447 |

**Verdicts (pre-registered arms, review P1 item 3):**

1. **Trace is THE dominant industrial mechanism: 3.8× at flagship
   capacity** — it GREW from the 2.03× measured pre-ladder. My
   stated worry that it would compress at scale like the kernel
   members was wrong in the opposite direction: mechanisms scale
   individually, not uniformly. The honest mechanism ranking at
   flagship now reads: trace 3.8× ≫ capacity (the frontier) ≫
   members ≈ 0–8% ≈ nothing.
2. **The two trace sub-mechanisms are near-perfect substitutes**:
   correction-only and readouts-only land within 0.1% of each other,
   each recovering ~96% of the log-gap; both together add ~6%.
   Mechanistic reading: what the model fundamentally needs is a
   channel carrying boundary self-identification ("this query IS the
   boundary at its own panel") — the exact jump constant and the
   learned readouts both deliver it, and once either does, the
   other is largely redundant. Design implication for #55 and any
   future variant: preserve at least one such channel; the exact
   correction is the principled zero-parameter choice.
3. Both mechanisms stay ON in the default (the +6% is free at
   inference).

**allbc canary readings (fork-managed, ep~105):** the
balanced-pooling arm trains STABLY at full LR where the raw
all-boundary arm diverged at ep44 (val 0.0170 at ep105); the raw
arm at LR/2 trains but poorly (0.0359). The reviewer's structural

## 2026-07-20 (evening) — balanced pooling stabilizes the all-boundary arm; fleet pre-registration; record corrections {#sec-nb-allbc-launch}

**A science observation arrived before the experiment proper:**
the all-boundary arm at flagship capacity DIVERGES at epoch 44
(train loss 2.7e17) at the family-standard LR — the 5-boundary
source set's measure imbalance inflates the attention-moment scale,
the same stability class as the ×4-width LR wall. Two fixes tested
as canaries: halving LR (raw arm trains, ep105 val 0.036), or
**balancing the per-boundary pool** — a per-sample measure offset
(effective log-gain g_s + ln Ā − ln A_s, dimensionless ratio,
similarity covariance untouched) so zero-init gains weight
boundaries equally instead of by raw area. **The balanced arm
trains at FULL standard LR** (ep105 val 0.017, ~2× better than the
LR-halved raw arm at matched epoch). The reviewer's structural
concern about measure dominance is thus tied to a hard
optimization failure, and the balance mechanism is itself the cure.
Implementation is a reparameterization, not a smaller hypothesis
class (identity test to 1e-9; gains can learn back the plain sum);
defaults bitwise, 540 tests.
